transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-11-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~85 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (PM), Maya (Eng Mgr), Ethan (SRE), Sofia (Product), Hannah (Release), Priya (CTO), Anil (QA), Claire (Ops), Mateo (Security), Rana (Legal)

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be rough): Roadmap sync for Q4 launch readiness. Discussed 11/10 outage root causes, outstanding canary & rollback actions, perf benchmark gaps on dedicated config, and compliance checklist. Assigned owners for post-mortem, benchmarks, runbooks, and launch comms.

--- TRANSCRIPT ---
[00:00] Jordan: alright let's get started, uh, thanks everyone for joining. we're a little long agenda but the big items are the 11/10 incident review, final perf benchmarks for Dedicated, and canary/rollout plan for private/vpc customers. Priya you wanted to open?
[00:12] Priya: yeah quick note - thanks team, I just want assurance that the post-mortem covers both the runtime failure and the orchestration flake, and that we have a clear communication plan for customers on dedicated reservations. we don't need a long preamble, just concrete owners.
[00:29] Maya: yeah, i can start with the root cause summary; quick caveat that some of my wording in the doc was, um, auto-corrected weirdly - so there may be a few typos. root cause was a combination of a kernel selector mismatch after the 11/09 rolling change and an unexpected KV cash (kv cash) invalidation that caused p99 latency spikes under certain seq lengths.
[00:52] Ethan: to add, the orchestration side had a brief controller race when scaling down, which left a subset of requests routed to a stale model variant. so two parallel failures: kernel selection wrong pair + routing race. that produced a spike, about 6 minutes of elevated errors, about 0.8% of requests affected.
[01:14] Anil: QA caught it in staging but did not reproduce at scale. we need a stronger staging load profile to hit the seq length distribution that triggered the kv cash issue.
[01:24] Jordan: note, "kv cash" in the notes - we should keep consistent term "KV cache" in the docs; small transcription slip. ok, what's the remediation timeline? Ethan?
[01:35] Ethan: immediate fix we pushed was a rollback of the kernel selector changes and a patch that rejects stale variant routing during scale-down. fixes are in canary, rolling to prod after validation. i estimate full roll to prod by tomorrow evening if benchmarks pass.
[01:50] Hannah: speaking of canary, the plan we discussed - canary 10% traffic for 1 hour, monitor p50/p95/p99, and if error rate > 0.2% or p99 regression > 20% then roll back. we also set manual holdpoints at each step. question: do we want automated rollback or manual?
[02:09] Sofia: i'd prefer manual for the first rollout then evaluate automations. we can't have another surprise.
[02:16] Priya: agreed manual initially. also legal/security need to prep a brief advisory for any impacted enterprise customers, including a timeline and root cause summary. Rana?
[02:28] Rana: yes, we'll draft a customer advisory; need the post-mortem items finalized first. we'll want to avoid technical jargon in the customer note; ops/eng can provide a technical appendix.
[02:40] Mateo: security side - no indicators of data exfil, but audit logs were incomplete for the scale-down window. we need to patch agent telemetry to capture that event type. i'll add that to action items.
[02:52] Jordan: good. switching to benchmarks - Maya, what's the status on Dedicated perf numbers?
[02:56] Maya: current numbers are close but we have a discrepancy in multi-stream throughput when we enable continuous batching + quantization profile A. p95 is fine but p99 is drifting up under long-seq tails. i'm running more runs tonight with longer seq distributions, and i've asked Platform to bump kernel timeouts. i'll post the sheet.
[03:18] Jordan: can you scope what "close" means in percent?
[03:21] Maya: sure, p50 about 5% slower vs baseline target, p95 about 8-10% slower, p99 about 15-22% depending on model and seq length. so it's noticeable at tail.
[03:32] Ethan: that tail behavior is likely tied to the KV cache invalidation timing; we saw similar symptoms in the incident. so the bench needs to replicate the exact seq length histogram. otherwise we're not validating the fix.
[03:44] Anil: i'll update QA load generator to include those histograms and run overnight.
[03:49] Hannah: for launch readiness checklist - i want a clear gating criteria doc: QA signoff, perf thresholds met, runbooks in place, canary plan approved, and exec sign-off. who's owning the gate? Jordan?
[04:02] Jordan: i'll own the gate internally; but big if: if p99 is above threshold we push. Also need security sign-off.
[04:10] Mateo: i'll confirm security checklist by Friday.
[04:14] Sofia: marketing timing - we can't promise date until gate green. but we should prep messaging now. i'll coordinate with marketing to have draft copy ready.
[04:25] Priya: for Private/VPC onboarding, what are the outstanding infra milestones? Claire?
[04:30] Claire: VPC templates need a final pass for KMS key management and audit log exports. we also need to validate HSM integration for a pilot customer. timelines are tight but feasible this week pending security sign-off.
[04:45] Ethan: note that dedicated capacity rollout has an ops cost consideration; autoscale policies must be tuned so we don't overcommit GPUs during canary. that's part of the cost/perf tradeoff we've been discussing.
[04:56] Jordan: ok let's capture risks: 1) p99 tail regressions still unresolved, 2) canary automation vs manual, 3) incomplete audit logs, 4) marketing date slip. any others?
[05:07] Maya: dependency on kernel selector code path being stable - if that toggles again during rollout we risk recurrence. need codeguard.
[05:14] Ethan: also capacity - if a partner runs a heavy benchmark we could saturate Dedicated pools. recommend temporary quota limits during initial launch.
[05:24] Priya: please put quota limits in recommendation document.
[05:28] Jordan: action items, we'll read them out. Ethan?
[05:31] Ethan: i will finalize the post-mortem doc, include timeline, exact RPC traces, and mitigation steps. posting by Tue 11/24.
[05:39] Maya: i'll post perf benchmark sheet by Sun 11/22 and run additional long-seq tests.
[05:45] Hannah: canary plan done by Mon 11/23 and schedule kickoff Wed 11/24 09:00 PT.
[05:52] Sofia: launch notes and marketing draft by Fri 11/25.
[05:56] Mateo: security artifact list and audit patch plan by Fri 11/27.
[06:00] Anil: QA sign-off smoke tests by Tue 11/24.
[06:04] Jordan: ok, quick tempo check - anything blocking these owners?
[06:09] Claire: HSM vendor needs final paperwork but legal says it's low risk; Rana can confirm.
[06:15] Rana: I'll follow up on vendor contracts today.
[06:18] Priya: i'd like daily 15-min stand for the next three days during the rollout window to keep tight coordination. good?
[06:24] Jordan: yes let's do 15-min sync at 08:30 PT starting 11/23 through 11/25. Hannah you'll calendar.
[06:31] Hannah: already on it.
[06:34] Maya: one more technical ask - can we add a short checklist to the runbook to verify kernel selector values and KV cache sanity before canary? that would've prevented the incident.
[06:45] Ethan: agreed. i'm adding pre-canary checks: kernel selector hash, live KV cache hit rate, and trace sampling at 1% for first 10 minutes.
[06:55] Jordan: good. last: communications. Sofia and Rana coordinate customer advisory and technical appendix. include a simple FAQ.
[07:05] Sofia: will do. also will coordinate with support on canned responses.
[07:10] Jordan: any other business?
[07:12] Mateo: small note - we should add improved telemetry for audit events related to scaling, i'll file a ticket after this call.
[07:18] Anil: testing note - i'll run the staging long-seq tests tonight and post results.
[07:22] Priya: cool. thanks team.
[07:25] Jordan: thanks everyone we'll follow up on the action items and meet in the 15-miners tomorrow. meeting adjourned.

END TRANSCRIPT
